vsm1.8:24.1:
When he does his recollecting in this way by comparing himself with others possessed of such great fame,
etc., in the light of the universality of death, thinking, “Death will come to me even as it
did to those distinguished beings,” then his meditation subject reaches access.
vsm1.8:24.2: This is how death should be recollected by comparison.
vsm1.8:25.1: 4. As to the sharing of the body with many: this body is shared by many.
vsm1.8:25.2: Firstly, it is shared by the eighty families of worms.
vsm1.8:25.3:
There too, creatures live in dependence on the outer skin, feeding on the outer skin; creatures live in dependence on the inner
skin, feeding on the inner skin; creatures live in dependence on the flesh, feeding on the flesh;
creatures live in dependence on the sinews, feeding on the sinews; creatures live in dependence on the bones,
feeding on the bones; and creatures live in dependence on the marrow, feeding on the marrow.
vsm1.8:25.4: And there they are born, grow old and die, evacuate, and make water;
vsm1.8:25.5: and the body is their maternity home, their hospital, their charnel-ground, their privy and their urinal.
vsm1.8:25.6: The body can also be brought to death with the upsetting of these worms.
vsm1.8:25.7:
And just as it is shared with the eighty families of worms, so too it is shared by the several hundred internal
diseases, as well as by such external causes of death as snakes, scorpions, and what not.
vsm1.8:26.1:
And just as when a target is set up at a crossroads and then arrows, spears, pikes, stones, etc.,
come from all directions and fall upon it, so too all kinds of accidents befall the body,
vsm1.8:26.2: and it also comes to death through these accidents befalling it.
vsm1.8:26.4:
“Here, bhikkhus, when day is departing and night is drawing on, a bhikkhu considers thus: ‘In many ways I can risk death.
A snake may bite me, or a scorpion may sting me, or a centipede may sting me. I might die of that, and that would set me
back. Or I might stumble and fall, or the food I have eaten might disagree with me, or my bile might get upset, or my phlegm
might get upset and sever my joints as it were like knives. I might die of that, and that would set me back’” (A III 306).
vsm1.8:26.5: That is how death should be recollected as to sharing the body with many.
vsm1.8:27.1: 5. As to the frailty of life: this life is impotent and frail.
vsm1.8:27.2:
For the life of beings is bound up with breathing, it is bound up with the postures, it is bound
up with cold and heat, it is bound up with the primary elements, and it is bound up with nutriment.
vsm1.8:28.1: Life occurs only when the in-breaths and out-breaths occur evenly.
vsm1.8:28.2:
But when the wind in the nostrils that has gone outside does not go in again, or when that which has gone
inside does not come out again, then a man is reckoned to be dead.
vsm1.8:28.3: And it occurs only when the four postures are found occurring evenly.
vsm1.8:28.4: But with the prevailing of anyone of them the life process is interrupted.
vsm1.8:28.5: And it occurs only when cold and heat are found occurring evenly.
vsm1.8:28.6: But it fails when a man is overcome by excessive cold or heat.
vsm1.8:28.7: And it occurs only when the four primary elements are found occurring evenly.
vsm1.8:28.8:
But with the disturbance of the earth element even a strong man’s life can be terminated if his body becomes
rigid, or with the disturbance of one of the elements beginning with water if his body becomes flaccid and petrified with a flux
of the bowels, etc., or if he is consumed by a bad fever, or if he suffers a severing of his limb-joint ligatures (cf. XI.102).
vsm1.8:28.9: And life occurs only in one who gets physical nutriment at the proper time; but if he gets none, he uses his life up.
vsm1.8:28.10: This is how death should be recollected as to the frailty of life.
vsm1.8:29.1: 6. As signless: as indefinable. The meaning is that it is unpredictable.
vsm1.8:29.2: For in the case of all beings:
vsm1.8:29.3:
“The span, the sickness, and the time, and where
The body will be laid, the destiny:
The living world can never know these things;
There is no sign foretells when they will be.
vsm1.8:30.1: Herein, firstly the span has no sign because there is no definition such as: Just so much must be lived, no more than that.
vsm1.8:30.2:
For beings die in the various stages of the embryo, namely, at the time of the kalala, of the abbuda, of the pesi,
of the ghana, at one month gone, two months gone, three months gone, four months gone, five months gone … ten months gone,
vsm1.8:30.3: and on the occasion of coming out of the womb.
vsm1.8:30.4: And after that they die this side or the other of the century.
vsm1.8:31.1: And the sickness has no sign because there is no definition such as: Beings die only of this sickness, not of any other.
vsm1.8:31.2: For beings die of eye disease or of any one among those beginning with ear disease (see A V 110).
vsm1.8:32.1: And the time has no sign because there is no definition such as: One has to die only at this time, not at any other.
vsm1.8:32.2: For beings die in the morning and at any of the other times such as noon.
vsm1.8:33.1:
And where the body will be laid down has no sign because there is no definition such as: When
people die, they must drop their bodies only here, not anywhere else.
vsm1.8:33.2: For the person of those born inside a village is dropped outside the village,
vsm1.8:33.3: and that of those born outside the village is dropped inside it.
vsm1.8:33.4:
Likewise that of those born in water is dropped on land, and that of those born
on land in water. And this can be multiplied in many ways.
vsm1.8:34.1: And the destiny has no sign because there is no definition such as: One who dies there must be reborn here.
vsm1.8:34.2:
For there are some who die in a divine world and are reborn in the human world, and there are some
who die in the human world and are reborn in a divine world, and so on.
vsm1.8:34.3: And in this way the world goes round and round the five kinds of destinies like an ox harnessed to a machine.
vsm1.8:34.4: This is how death should be recollected as signless.
vsm1.8:35.1: 7. As to the limitedness of the extent: the extent of human life is short now.
vsm1.8:35.2: One who lives long lives a hundred years, more or less.
vsm1.8:35.4:
“Bhikkhus, this human life span is short. There is a new life to be gone to, there are profitable deeds to be done,
there is the life of purity to be led. There is no not dying for the born. He who lives long lives a hundred years, more or less …”
vsm1.8:35.6:
And he said further: “Bhikkhus, there was once a teacher called Araka …” (A IV 136),
all of which sutta should be given in full, adorned as it is with seven similes.
vsm1.8:36.1:
And he said further: “Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu develops mindfulness of death thus, ‘Oh, let me live
a night and day that I may attend to the Blessed One’s teaching, surely much could be done by me,’
vsm1.8:36.2:
and when a bhikkhu develops mindfulness of death thus, ‘Oh, let me live a day that I may
attend to the Blessed One’s teaching, surely much could be done by me,’
vsm1.8:36.3:
and when a bhikkhu develops mindfulness of death thus, ‘Oh, let me live as long as it takes to chew and swallow
four or five mouthfuls that I may attend to the Blessed One’s teaching, surely much could be done by me’—
vsm1.8:36.4: these are called bhikkhus who dwell in negligence and slackly develop mindfulness of death for the destruction of cankers.
vsm1.8:37.1:
“And, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu develops mindfulness of death thus, ‘Oh, let me live for as long as it takes to chew and swallow
a single mouthful that I may attend to the Blessed One’s teaching, surely much could be done by me,’
vsm1.8:37.2:
and when a bhikkhu develops mindfulness of death thus, ‘Oh, let me live as long as it takes to breathe in and breathe out, or as
long as it takes to breathe out and breathe in, that I may attend to the Blessed One’s teaching, surely much could be done by me’—
vsm1.8:37.3:
these are called bhikkhus who dwell in diligence and keenly develop
mindfulness of death for the destruction of cankers” (A III 305–6).
vsm1.8:38.1:
So short in fact is the extent of life that it is not certain even for as long as it takes to chew and swallow
four or five mouthfuls. This is how death should be recollected as to the limitedness of the extent.
vsm1.8:39.1:
8. As to the shortness of the moment: in the ultimate sense the life-moment of living beings
is extremely short, being only as much as the occurrence of a single conscious moment.
vsm1.8:39.2:
Just as a chariot wheel, when it is rolling, rolls that is, touches the ground only on one point of the circumference of its tire,
and, when it is at rest, rests only on one point, so too, the life of living beings lasts only for a single conscious moment.
vsm1.8:39.3: When that consciousness has ceased, the being is said to have ceased,
vsm1.8:39.5:
“In a past conscious moment he did live, not he does live, not he will live. In a future conscious moment not he did live,
not he does live, he will live. In the present conscious moment not he did live, he does live, not he will live.
vsm1.8:39.6:
“Life, person, pleasure, pain—just these alone
Join in one conscious moment that flicks by.
vsm1.8:39.7:
Ceased aggregates of those dead or alive
Are all alike, gone never to return.
vsm1.8:39.8:
“No world is born if consciousness is not
Produced; when that is present, then it lives;
When consciousness dissolves, the world is dead:
The highest sense this concept will allow” (Nidd I 42).
vsm1.8:39.9: This is how death should be recollected as to the shortness of the moment.
vsm1.8:40.1:
So while he does his recollecting by means of one or other of these eight ways, his consciousness acquires
the support of repetition owing to the reiterated attention, mindfulness settles down with death as its object,
the hindrances are suppressed, and the jhāna factors make their appearance.
vsm1.8:40.2:
But since the object is stated with individual essences, and since it awakens a sense of urgency,
the jhāna does not reach absorption and is only access.
vsm1.8:40.3:
Now, with special development, the supramundane jhāna and the second and the fourth immaterial
jhānas reach absorption even with respect to states with individual essences.
vsm1.8:40.4: For the supramundane reaches absorption by means of progressive development of the purification
vsm1.8:40.5: and the immaterial jhānas do so by means of development consisting in the surmounting of the object (see Ch. X)
vsm1.8:40.6:
since there in those two immaterial jhānas there is merely the surmounting of the object of jhāna
that had already reached absorption.
vsm1.8:40.7: But here in mundane mindfulness of death there is neither
vsm1.8:40.8: so the jhāna only reaches access.
vsm1.8:40.9: And that access is known as “mindfulness of death” too since it arises through its means.
vsm1.8:41.1: A bhikkhu devoted to mindfulness of death is constantly diligent.
vsm1.8:41.2: He acquires perception of disenchantment with all kinds of becoming (existence).
vsm1.8:41.6: He has no stain of avarice about requisites.
vsm1.8:41.7: Perception of impermanence grows in him, following upon which there appear the perceptions of pain and not-self.
vsm1.8:41.8:
But while beings who have not developed mindfulness of death fall victims to fear,
horror and confusion at the time of death as though suddenly seized by wild beasts, spirits, snakes,
robbers, or murderers, he dies undeluded and fearless without falling into any such state.
vsm1.8:41.9: And if he does not attain the deathless here and now, he is at least headed for a happy destiny on the breakup of the body.
vsm1.8:41.10:
Now, when a man is truly wise,
His constant task will surely be
This recollection about death
Blessed with such mighty potency.
vsm1.8:41.11: This is the section dealing with the recollection of death in the detailed explanation.
